statement: Craigslist is a classified-advertisements platform: users browse, search, and filter community postings by region and category; open listing detail pages to inspect description, photos, price, location, and reply options; create and manage their own postings through a multi-step wizard (category, location, details, contact, photos, preview, publish); and manage them later through account login, posting history, edit/renew/repost/delete, saved searches, and favorites. The offline clone reproduces the anonymous public surface (region/category index, housing section, search with price/neighborhood/date/category filters, listing detail, reply and flagging entry points, help, sign-in/registration/password-recovery entry surfaces, branded not-found) plus the full stateful backend needed for registration, login, posting CRUD, persistence across refresh and re-login, per-user data isolation, deterministic seeds, and a no-results state.
out_of_scope: Real craigslist multi-region full corpus: only a curated region set is populated; other regions render the region shell with empty listings.
Real-world cross-site identity, real email delivery, real payments, and external network access: the clone is offline with a local mail outbox and local-sandbox effects.
Discussion forums, personals-adjacent content, jobs/services/gigs full verticals: category shells exist but the populated catalog centers on housing with representative for-sale/community items.
Realtime chat, WebSockets, and third-party map tiles: map/location rendering uses local deterministic data with a truthful simulation label.

Source-side authenticated surfaces (posting wizard, account management) are implemented from the public PRD and inferred semantics because direct authenticated source evidence is unavailable; evidence grades are recorded accordingly.
Live reproduction of craigslist's dynamic timestamps and per-region moderation content: seeded deterministic data is used instead.
